question_text: The lengths of adult fish of a certain species are normally distributed with mean $40\text{ cm}$ and standard deviation $5\text{ cm}$.

subparts.stem: Find the probability that a randomly chosen adult fish of this species is longer than 45 cm.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up normal CDF calculation with $X \sim \text{N}(40, 5^2)$ for $P(X > 45)$

subparts.solution:
Let the length of a randomly selected adult fish be $X\text{ cm}$.

So, $X \sim \text{N}(40, 5^2)$.

$P(X > 45) \approx 0.159$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Calculating upper-tail probability for a normally distributed random variable.
step_by_step: Calculate $P(X > 45)$ using normal CDF with lower bound $45$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using variance $25$ instead of standard deviation $5$.

subparts.stem: Find the probability that a randomly chosen adult fish of this species is between 35 cm and 50 cm long.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up normal CDF calculation for $P(35 \le X \le 50)$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Calculating interval probability on a normal distribution.
step_by_step: Enter lower bound $35$ and upper bound $50$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Rounding errors from premature rounding of $z$-scores.

subparts.stem: Determine the minimum length of the longest 10% of this species of fish.
subparts.solution:
$P(X > l) = 0.1$

$\therefore P(X \le l) = 0.9$

$\therefore l = 46.4$

$\therefore$ the minimum length of the longest $10\%$ of fish is about $46.4\text{ cm}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Using the inverse normal distribution to find a boundary value corresponding to an upper tail area.
step_by_step: The longest $10\%$ corresponds to an upper tail of $0.1$, so cumulative area to the left is $1 - 0.1 = 0.9$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using area $= 0.1$ for a left-tail function directly without adjusting to $0.9$.

subparts.stem: A randomly selected fish is shorter than 48 cm. Find the probability that it is between 40 cm and 44 cm long.

step_by_step: Identify the intersection of $(40 \le X \le 44)$ and $(X < 48)$, which is simply $(40 \le X \le 44)$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Incorrectly taking the intersection as extending to 48 instead of 44.
